message.content: Two more pages: delivery-header reference for the ID semantics, and failed-delivery handling for retry scope.
message.reasoning_content:
Excellent. Key documented facts:

1. Signature: HMAC-SHA256 (X-Hub-Signature-256) over the raw payload; secret required; constant-time comparison; never plain ==; JSON parse/re-serialize before verification breaks verification because HMAC is computed over raw payload bytes. Docs show reading raw body (`request.body.read` / `await req.text()`), then verify, then parse. This is documented.

2. Delivery ID: X-GitHub-Delivery is same across redeliveries; "The GUID is constant across redeliveries of the same delivery." So the team's premise (new delivery identifier for redelivery) is wrong. Dedup must key on the GUID, not treat redelivery as new.

3. Timing: respond 2XX within 10 seconds; else GitHub terminates and considers the delivery failed. 25-second synchronous job violates this. Use queue/background processing, respond immediately.

4. Retry: "GitHub does not automatically redeliver failed deliveries" (redelivering webhooks page). Automated redelivery must be scripted (Actions workflow / cron) using REST API endpoints; deliveries retained 3 days; redelivery possible for past 3 days. So the ops plan assuming GitHub retries after outage is wrong.

Also delivery headers description for X-GitHub-Delivery. Let me fetch the webhook events and payloads page's delivery headers section to cite the definition, plus maybe the REST API endpoint docs for redeliver attempts / list deliveries (GitHub App? not needed). Also maybe the "handling failed webhook deliveries" page which describes failed delivery statuses and redelivery conditions. Let's fetch:
- https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#delivery-headers
- https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/handling-failed-webhook-deliveries
